subject: general
question: Why is it advised to clean your mouth after vomiting?

options.text: To neutralise the acid and protect tooth enamel
To stop the spread of infection

solution:
The correct answer is __**To neutralise the acid and protect tooth enamel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The primary reason for cleaning the mouth after vomiting is that vomit contains **Stomach Acid**, which is highly corrosive. This acid is mainly **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, which has a very low **pH** level, typically between **1.5 and 3.5**.
 
• **Tooth Enamel** is the hardest and most highly mineralized substance in the human body, but it is highly susceptible to damage from strong acids. Enamel begins to demineralize and dissolve when the **pH** in the mouth falls below a critical level of approximately **5.5**.
 
• When a person vomits, the **Hydrochloric Acid** from the stomach coats the teeth. If left uncleaned, this acid causes **Dental Erosion** (also known as acid erosion), which is the irreversible loss of the protective tooth structure. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
